A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AIR-BENCH research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F are available and support reliable comparison, including the rotated appendix tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval evaluations, generated-versus-human benchmark consistency experiments, quality-control ablation, robustness analysis and domain-specific fine-tuning results.

after.justification: v4 retains original AIR-BENCH evaluations and fine-tuning experiments, with revised model comparisons and consistency results in Tables 5–7 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: The three-stage pipeline, character/scenario generation, query rewriting, hard-negative generation and quality-control procedure remain unchanged, including their appendix specifications. New design motivations and temperature disclosure do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same QA and Long-Doc tasks, AIR-BENCH releases, 69 datasets, nine domains and 13 languages. The MS MARCO validation and domain-specific fine-tuning datasets are retained; appendix dataset specifications are unchanged.

E2.justification: The consistency comparison drops jina-embeddings-v2-base-en, reducing the evaluated set from 18 models in v1 Table 4 to 17 in v4 Table 5. The MTEB/AIR-BENCH comparison replaces multilingual-e5-large with jina-embeddings-v3 in v4 Table 6, although both appear elsewhere in the earlier paper.

E3.justification: The data splits, evaluation metrics, 512-token input limits, fine-tuning budgets and 2,000-query subsampling procedure remain unchanged. The newly stated generation temperature is additional disclosure. The BGE zero-shot labels added to the main comparison were already present in v1 Table 22.

E4.justification: The quality-control ablation retains its question about agreement with human labels but removes the jina-embeddings-v2-base-en comparison. Figure 3 also revises the numerical robustness evidence. Instruction sensitivity, diversity analyses, domain/language comparisons and illustrative cases remain unchanged; no new analysis question is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report Spearman correlations and p-values and describe 30 simulated generation processes using random query subsamples. The mean correlation and mean p-value reporting practice is retained; revised numerical estimates do not introduce a new uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: With the reduced comparator set, consistency correlations change from 0.8204 to 0.8211 with quality control and from 0.7028 to 0.6912 without it, with corresponding p-value and ranking updates. Figure 3's mean correlation changes from 0.8067 to 0.8031. The MTEB comparison updates e5-mistral-7b-instruct's overall/retrieval scores from 66.63/56.89 to 66.40/56.87 and replaces one model's result row. These are revised reported results, not evidence of a same-setting improvement. Detailed appendix benchmark scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The retrieval formulation, set definitions and mathematical description of the generation and quality-control pipeline are unchanged. Section 2.5 adds conceptual motivations rather than formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: automated, heterogeneous and dynamic retrieval evaluation, agreement with human-labeled evaluation, and discrimination between model capabilities. The reported scope of those contributions is unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 2.5 explains the proposed benefits of real-world corpora, character/scenario generation, rewriting and hard negatives. The limitations are substantively softened: specific instruction-following, domain and language dependencies are replaced by broader discussion, and v4 suggests model progress can mitigate capability limits and evaluation bias without adding supporting experiments.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 newly specifies a GPT-4 sampling temperature of 1.0. The generator version was already disclosed in v1 Appendix A and is moved into the main text. Prompts, preprocessing details, hardware, computational-budget estimates and principal code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 3.3 explicitly discusses positioning against MTEB/C-MTEB saturation and support for emerging-domain evaluation; Section 2.5 connects quality control to MIRACL relevance assessment. The Günther et al. (2023) Jina embeddings 2 reference is removed. The broader related-work coverage and novelty claim remain stable.

P1.justification: v4 adds design-motivation and positioning subsections, consolidates overview and diversity discussion under Section 3, adds an appendix guide and acknowledgements, and rewrites the limitations. Author information and several cross-references are updated, while most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 4–6 are reordered and renumbered, comparison-table membership changes, and Figure 3 is updated and relocated. Appendix material is repaginated, including placing the news example on a separate page. The main diagrams, supplementary chart structures and detailed dataset/result tables retain their presentation.

improvement.justification: The added design explanations, clearer navigation and explicit sampling temperature modestly improve understanding and reproducibility. The scientific evidence remains largely unchanged. These gains are limited by the more optimistic limitations discussion, which suggests future model improvements will mitigate bias without new validation; the revision does not resolve that underlying concern.
